map.隧道瓦斯监测参考 使用指南: Tunnel Gas Monitoring Reference User Guide
map.输入瓦斯浓度，查询安全等级与处置措施（依据《煤矿安全规程》《铁路瓦斯隧道技术规范: Enter the gas concentration to look up the safety grade and response measures (based on the 'Coal Mine Safety Regulations' and the 'Technical Code for Railway Gas Tunnels')
map.五级浓度分级与处置：<0.5% 安全（正常作业、持续监测）、0.5%~0.8%: Five-level concentration grading and response: <0.5% safe (normal work, continuous monitoring), 0.5%-0.8% caution (increase ventilation and monitoring frequency), 0.8%-1.0% alert (stop part of the work, withdraw non-essential personnel), 1.0%-1.5% danger (stop work, cut power, withdraw personnel), >=1.5% extreme danger (evacuate immediately, seal the working face, report for handling).
map.断电阈值：浓度达到或超过 1.0% 即判需立即切断电源；页面按监测位置（工作面/: Power-cut threshold: reaching or exceeding 1.0% means power must be cut immediately; the page marks monitoring points by location (working face/return airflow, general roadway, near electrical equipment), and all three thresholds are 1.0%.
map.爆炸性判定：浓度落在 5%~16% 区间判为处于爆炸浓度范围（极度危险）；低于: Explosiveness judgement: a concentration in the 5%-16% range is judged to be within the explosive range (extremely dangerous); below 5% is under the lower explosive limit and will not explode; above 16% is over the upper explosive limit and will not explode for lack of oxygen. The page shows the current interval with a five-segment colour bar (safe green / caution blue / alert yellow / danger red / extreme danger dark red).
map.算例：八个浓度点的分级与处置判定: Worked example: grading and response judgement for eight concentration points
map.：0.30% → 安全、正常作业持续监测、不断电、低于爆炸下限；0.50% →: : 0.30% -> safe, normal work with continuous monitoring, no power cut, below the lower explosive limit; 0.50% -> caution, increase ventilation and monitoring frequency, no power cut; 0.65% -> caution, same as above; 0.90% -> alert, stop part of the work and withdraw non-essential personnel, no power cut (has not reached 1.0%); 1.20% -> danger, stop work, cut power, withdraw personnel, power cut required; 2.00% -> extreme danger, evacuate immediately, seal the working face and report, power cut required; 8.00% -> extreme danger and within the explosive concentration range (5%-16%); 20.00% -> extreme danger, but above the upper explosive limit so it will not explode for lack of oxygen.
map.为什么规定瓦斯浓度达到 1.0% 就要断电撤人？: Why do the rules require cutting power and withdrawing people when gas concentration reaches 1.0%?
map.1.0% 远低于 5% 的爆炸下限，留出的余量用于应对监测滞后、局部积聚与浓度快: 1.0% is far below the 5% lower explosive limit, and the margin covers monitoring lag, local accumulation and rapid rises in concentration. Gas distribution underground is extremely uneven, and the roof, corners and stopped-airflow zones easily form local high concentrations, so when a monitoring point reads 1.0% the local level may already be far higher. That is why the rules require stopping work, cutting power and withdrawing personnel at 1.0%, ventilating first and re-testing until it passes before resuming, rather than waiting until it approaches the lower explosive limit.
map.浓度超过 16% 反而「不爆炸」，是不是就不危险了？: If the concentration exceeds 16% it 'will not explode' instead, so is it no longer dangerous?
map.不是。高于爆炸上限只是意味着该处混合气体因缺氧而无法被点燃，但极其危险：一是人员: No. Being above the upper explosive limit only means the mixture at that spot cannot be ignited because of lack of oxygen, but it is extremely dangerous: first, anyone entering can suffocate from lack of oxygen; second, once the gas mixes with fresh air and is diluted back into the 5%-16% range it instantly becomes an explosive mixture. Therefore high-concentration gas accumulation zones must be sealed off and entry strictly forbidden, and handling is done by a professional rescue team following gas drainage procedures with slow release and continuous monitoring of return airflow concentration.

map.输入瓦斯浓度，查询安全等级与处置措施（依据《煤矿安全规程》《铁路瓦斯隧道技术规范: User guide for Tunnel Gas Monitoring Reference: how to use this free browser-based tool, including key inputs, step-by-step instructions, worked examples, FAQs and practical notes.
map.本工具纯前端运行，输入内容不上传服务器；结果为按上述口径得到的理论估算值。实际应: This tool runs entirely in your browser and uploads nothing. Results are theoretical estimates under the stated assumptions. Actual work depends on equipment, measurement conditions and local standards; verify against nameplates, test reports and current standards, and consult a professional for major decisions.
map.按瓦斯浓度、监测位置、氧含量与可配置阈值给出参考分级；5%~16% 是否可爆须结: Classify by methane concentration, monitoring location, oxygen level and configurable thresholds. Whether 5%–16% can explode depends on oxygen and ignition source; a single concentration is never asserted safe.
map.可配置阈值：报警阈值与撤人/断电阈值由用户填写，默认 0.5%/1.0% 仅为示: Configurable thresholds: alarm and evacuation/power-cut thresholds are entered by the user; defaults 0.5%/1.0% are examples only. The page gives “below alarm / alarm / evacuation-power cut / high-concentration high-risk” reference levels instead of hard-coding one regional code as universal.
map.位置与测点：工作面/回风流、一般巷道、电气设备附近分别标注；单次测点不能代表全断: Location and measurement points: working face/return airway, general roadway and near electrical equipment are labelled separately. One reading cannot represent the whole section; local accumulation, roof and corner pockets, and stopped-air zones can distort readings, so multiple points are needed.
map.氧含量与爆炸条件：5%~16% 只是甲烷爆炸浓度范围；是否形成爆炸三角还取决于氧: Oxygen and explosion conditions: 5%–16% is only the methane explosive concentration range. Whether the explosion triangle exists also depends on oxygen (a common criterion is ≥12%) and an ignition source. Oxygen may be left blank; the page then does not assert explosible or non-explosible.
map.完整量程：色条覆盖 0–100 %VOL，包括 5%~16% 爆炸浓度范围与高于: Full range: the bars cover 0–100 %VOL, including 5%–16% and above 16%; no concentration is directly asserted “safe”.
map.算例：不同浓度与氧含量下的参考判定：默认报警 0.5%、撤人/断电 1.0%、O: Example: reference classification at different concentrations and oxygen levels — Defaults: alarm 0.5%, evacuation/power cut 1.0%, O₂=20.9%. 0.30% is below alarm but still requires monitoring; 0.50% reaches alarm and prompts more ventilation and preparation to evacuate; 0.90% remains alarm; 1.20% reaches the evacuation/power-cut threshold; 8.00% lies in 5%–16% with O₂ ≥12%, close to the concentration and oxygen conditions of the explosion triangle, so treat as extremely high risk. The same 8.00% with O₂=10% lacks the common oxygen condition but remains an oxygen-deficiency hazard and may enter the explosive range after dilution. 20.00% is above the upper explosive limit; concentration alone cannot show it will not asphyxiate or ignite, so seal and evacuate.
map.为什么不能只看一个 1.0% 阈值就下结论？: Why can’t I conclude from a single 1.0% threshold?
map.不同地区、工况、巷道类型与设备类别的报警、撤人、断电要求可能不同，现场还受测点代: Alarm, evacuation and power-cut requirements can differ by region, condition, roadway type and equipment class. On site, measurement representativeness, ventilation, oxygen and ignition sources also matter. The page makes thresholds configurable and labels them as examples for professionals to set under the applicable code; the result is a reference classification, not an enforcement or response basis.
map.浓度高于 16% 是不是就不爆炸、可以进入？: Does methane above 16% mean no explosion and safe entry?
map.绝对不能。高于爆炸上限只说明该混合气在当前氧含量下可能无法被点燃，但高浓度瓦斯可: Absolutely not. Above the upper explosive limit only means the mixture may not ignite at the current oxygen level; high methane can still cause asphyxiation, and mixing with fresh air may bring it back into 5%–16% and form an explosive mixture. Seal the area, evacuate, and let a professional rescue team handle it while monitoring the return airway.
